channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: WTI slips below $74 after recent rally, Middle East tensions limit the downside
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) trades lower on Thursday and hovers around $73.10 at the time of writing, down 1.95% on the day as investors take profits following two consecutive days of strong gains.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Slips despite yield support – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research economist Philip Wee notes the US Dollar Index (DXY) slipped from 101.28 to 101 late in the US session, even as the US Treasury 2Y yield rose and crude Oil stayed supported by Middle East tensions.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Thursday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $59.17 per troy ounce, up 1.45% from the $58.32 it cost on Wednesday.

item.title: Euro advances against Canadian Dollar on strong German trade, weak oil
item.description: EUR/CAD gains ground after two days of losses, trading around 1.6210 during the European hours on Thursday. The currency cross remains stronger following stronger-than-expected trade data from Germany.

item.title: Euro: ECB hawkish repricing with bond selloff – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank Research’s Early Morning Reid notes that European assets are sensitive to the renewed energy shock. Market pricing for ECB hikes by December rose sharply, implying a chance of three hikes this year after June’s move.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Fed hawks supported by energy spike – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes that higher Oil prices and Gulf tensions have driven a bigger reaction in rates than in FX, with Brent near $80 supporting Fed hawks. The US Dollar (USD) is expected to stay firm versus low-yielders, while carry trades in Emerging Markets (EM) have been unwound.

item.title: US Dollar: Constructive outlook as Oil risks build – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note renewed Middle East tensions and higher Oil prices are lifting the US Dollar (USD) and global bond yields.

item.title: Australian Dollar steadies above 0.6900 as markets price a negotiated end to Iran’s war
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) keeps trading sideways against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, showing a surprising resilience to the escalating tensions in Iran.

item.title: Gold clings to gains on weaker USD; bearish bias remains amid Iran risks, Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its bid tone above the $4,100 mark through the first half of the European session on Thursday and looks to build on the previous day's bounce from a one-week low.

item.title: Japanese Yen remains pressured close to 40-year lows as intervention risks linger
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) remains locked in a high-stakes standoff against the US Dollar, testing the ultimate limits of Tokyo’s tolerance for its local currency to depreciate.

item.title: Indian Rupee bounces back as investors digest higher oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday. The USD/INR pair drops to near 95.40 as the US Dollar ticks lower; however, the outlook of the pair remains bullish as renewed Middle East hostilities have boosted oil prices.

item.title: Dow Jones futures advance due to tech, AI rally
item.description: Dow Jones futures gain 0.17% to trade around 52,710 during European trading hours on Thursday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq 100 futures advance 0.34% and 0.74%, trading near 7,550 and 29,690, respectively.

item.title: United States Dollar Index Price Forecast: Flirts with 23.6% Fibo./weekly low below 101.00
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, extends the previous day's pullback from the 101.25-101.30 region and attracts some follow-through sellers on Thursday.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains against US Dollar despite renewed geopolitical risks
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) trades higher against the US Dollar (USD) despite renewed geopolitical risks.

item.title: Euro: Early gains against US Dollar at risk on Fed story – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING highlights that EUR/USD has held up despite higher Oil, as Euro swap rates outperformed US rates on expectations of an ECB hike in September. However, he argues the Fed narrative will dominate, with EUR/USD likely to surrender gains and fall below 1.14.

item.title: Japan’s Kihara says government aims to secure market trust by stably lowering debt-to-GDP ratio
item.description: Japan's Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said during the European trading session on Thursday that the administration wants to secure market trust by stably lowering the government debt-to-GDP ratio.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Euro wavers around 1.1430 with the bearish trend intact
item.description: The Euro (EUR) posts moderate gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, hitting session highs near 1.1440, yet trapped within the weekly range, with the broader bearish trend in play.

item.title: British Pound extends rally vs JPY; climbs to fresh high since January 2008
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross builds on the previous day's strong positive momentum and gains traction for the second successive day on Thursday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Tentative upside risk above 0.6980 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang sees AUD/USD confined to a 0.6915–0.6950 intraday range as momentum remains lacklustre. For 1–3 weeks, upward momentum is tentatively building, with rising risk of a break above 0.6980 while 0.6900 acts as strong support.

item.title: Forex Today: Markets overlook escalating tensions in Middle East
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Thursday, July 9:

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Firm as RBNZ signals more tightening – DBS
item.description: Philip Wee from DBS Group Research reports NZD/USD is holding firm above 0.57 after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand unanimously voted to lift the Official Cash Rate by 25 bps to 2.50%, a shift from May’s split decision.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Hovers above 1.4150 as bullish bias prevails
item.description: USD/CAD moves sideways after two days of losses, trading around 1.4170 during the European hours on Thursday. The technical analysis of the daily chart indicates the pair is remaining within the ascending channel pattern, indicating a persistent bullish bias.

item.title: Oil: Rising geopolitical risks and Russian diesel ban – ING
item.description: ING analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note that Oil has extended its rally as renewed US-Iran tensions threaten the fragile ceasefire and disrupt flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Qatar condemns Iran's attacks on ships, urges parties to commit to MoU
item.description: In a released statement from Qatar Prime Minister (PM) Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani after a phone call with Iranian Foreign Minister (FM) Abbas Araghchi, AI Thani said that he discussed about latest military escalation in the Middle East between the United States (US) and Iran and condem

item.title: Euro: Hawkish Fed keeps gains contained against US Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Thu Lan Nguyen at Commerzbank notes that EUR/USD has traded in a narrow range and appears largely unaffected by Iran-related headlines, as the correlation with Oil has weakened.

item.title: US Dollar: Supported by higher yields and FOMC stance – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan reports that June Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes show policymakers increasingly concerned that US inflation could stay elevated, with some seeing a case for a rate hike.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Dollar bulls lose steam after rejection at 0.8100
item.description: The US Dollar is trading lower against the Swiss Franc (CHF) on Thursday, as investors ponder the consequences of reciprocal US and Iran attacks and a 10% rebound in Oil prices, on the major central banks' monetary policies.

item.title: Euro holds gains against Japanese Yen as Germany’s Trade Surplus widens in May
item.description: EUR/JPY extends its gains for the second successive day, trading around 185.70 during the early European hours on Thursday. The currency cross maintains its upward momentum following stronger-than-expected seasonally-adjusted Trade Balance data from Germany.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Downside bias but mixed outlook – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes USD/JPY retains an upside bias, with scope for a test of 162.80 intraday while major resistance at 163.00 is unlikely to be reached. Over 1–3 weeks, the outlook is mixed, with trading expected between 160.60 and 163.00.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD jumps to near $59 as US Dollar declines
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) is up over 1% to near $59.00 during the European trading session on Thursday. The white metal gains as the US Dollar (USD) faces selling pressure despite multiple tailwinds.
